recommendation: Keep the empty no-change audit commit. Core FHIR already reflects FHIR-22994; future requests for clinical-research specificity should be handled in IG profiles, extensions, or separate terminology work rather than re-expanding the core example value set.
issue_request: FHIR-22994 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for Patient Care and requested that the AdverseEvent.seriousness example value set include only serious and non-serious, avoiding older FDA outcome-style child codes that confused seriousness with AdverseEvent.outcome.
initial_application: The Jira-linked 2019 commit 05acdd8 removed the former serious-results-in-death, serious-is-life-threatening, serious-results-in-hospitalization, serious-results-in-disability, serious-is-birth-defect, and serious-requires-prevent-impairment codes from the then-authoritative AdverseEvent spreadsheet and added the requested definitions for serious and non-serious.
additional_context: AdverseEvent is active in source/fhir.ini. The current StructureDefinition keeps AdverseEvent.seriousness as an example binding to the Adverse Event Seriousness value set, whose compose includes the THO adverse-event-seriousness code system. The current THO code system contains exactly non-serious and serious. Later Patient Care decisions FHIR-23023 and FHIR-48544, plus Patient Care minutes from 2021 and 2022, support keeping seriousness separate from outcome and leaving IG-specific criteria to profiles or other terminology.
reconciliation: No source change was made because the current build-scoped core source plus current THO terminology already implement the published two-code decision and no old outcome-style seriousness codes remain in current core source.

related_jiras.note: The same 2019 application commit also removed AdverseEvent.severity and clarified seriousness versus severity; it is already represented separately on the combined branch.
Patient Care rejected adding overdose/cancer seriousness values because FHIR-22994 reduced the value set to serious/non-serious and the binding is example.
A later R6 no-change decision kept AdverseEvent.seriousness as an example binding and cited FHIR-22994 as the reason outcome-like codes were removed.
